name: Flip the Cards
description: There is a deck of $$$n$$$ cards. The $$$i$$$-th card has a number $$$a_i$$$ on the front and a number $$$b_i$$$ on the back. Every integer between $$$1$$$ and $$$2n$$$ appears exactly once on the cards. A deck is called sorted if the front values are in increasing order and the back values are in decreasing order. That is, if $$$a_i \lt a_{i+1}$$$ and $$$b_i \gt b_{i+1}$$$ for all $$$1\le i \lt n$$$. To flip a card $$$i$$$ means swapping the values of $$$a_i$$$ and $$$b_i$$$. You must flip some subset of cards (possibly, none), then put all the cards in any order you like. What is the minimum number of cards you must flip in order to sort the deck?
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1\le n\le 2\cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of cards. The next $$$n$$$ lines describe the cards. The $$$i$$$-th of these lines contains two integers $$$a_i, b_i$$$ ($$$1\le a_i, b_i\le 2n$$$). Every integer between $$$1$$$ and $$$2n$$$ appears exactly once.
output_specification: If it is impossible to sort the deck, output " -1 ". Otherwise, output the minimum number of flips required to sort the deck.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1503D — Flip the Cards [34. Two Pointers]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
